title: Samsung TV Plus Tops 100 Million Users. What Pluto TV’s Slide Means for K-FAST
summary: Samsung TV Plus tops 100 million users amid shifting K-FAST market dynamics
detailed: Pluto TV loses users as Samsung TV Plus scales up and expands Korean programming.

sentences: Pluto TV loses users as Samsung TV Plus scales up and expands Korean programming.
Pluto TV, a pioneer of free ad-supported streaming television (FAST), is losing users as rivals expand.
In its third-quarter shareholder letter released on November 9, Skydance put Pluto TV’s monthly active users (MAUs) at approximately 75 million.
Samsung TV Plus, meanwhile, announced in January that it had surpassed 100 million monthly active users worldwide.
Its established TV distribution and growing Korean lineup provide a concrete route for K-FAST to reach audiences.
That is 14.6 million, or 16%, below the 89.6 million reported for 2025, and below the 80 million the company celebrated as a milestone in May 2023.
As competing services gain users and viewing share, control over the television home screen is becoming a defining advantage in FAST distribution.
For Korean FAST suppliers, the next task is turning channel launches into sustained viewing.
Pluto TV’s weakness lies less in demand for free television than in how it retains existing viewers and acquires new ones.
It changed a familiar channel-led experience while rivals expanded through on-demand viewing and TV home screens.
Interface friction is a possible near-term factor; the timing of its VOD response and its distribution position are structural explanations for the growth gap.
The most direct criticism concerns the redesign.
Two Paramount employees interviewed by Business Insider suggested that September’s shift toward on-demand discovery may have contributed to the decline.
Replacing an experience that opened into a playing channel with one centered on choosing content changed the routine of habitual channel surfers.
A second issue is the timing of its response to on-demand competition.
Pluto built its identity around scheduled channels while Tubi and YouTube grew around viewer choice.
Pluto’s comprehensive home-screen, search and recommendation rebuild arrived in September 2026.
Reported VOD growth shows demand for that offering, but more VOD use among some viewers is a different outcome from restoring the service’s total monthly audience.
Third is audience acquisition.
Roku, Samsung and LG can give their services visibility through devices or operating systems.
Without its own TV operating system, Pluto depends more on third-party placement and viewers actively choosing its app.
This is a distribution disadvantage in discovery and repeat visits, rather than evidence of a measured cause of every lost user.
Technology integration adds context.
Skydance said bringing Pluto and Paramount+ together took about 18 months, committing product and engineering capacity to a shared foundation while competitors kept developing their offerings.
Management says that foundation reduces costs and accelerates development; integration itself has not been established as a cause of the audience decline.
The central issue is therefore the execution of a transition: preserving effortless channel viewing while improving VOD and recommendations and finding new viewers on the TV screen.
Published data do not isolate each factor’s contribution or track the same users before and after the redesign.
September’s changes cannot explain the entire decline on their own.
For K-FAST, distribution agreements must be followed by a plan for discovery, return visits and viewing conversion.
Tom Ryan and Ilya Pozin founded Pluto TV in 2014, bringing cable-style channel surfing to free internet television.
Viacom acquired it in January 2019 for $340 million in cash.
The service passed through ViacomCBS and Paramount before becoming part of Skydance.
Rivals have moved in the opposite direction.
Fox-owned Tubi increased its monthly audience from 74 million in September 2023 to 110 million in August 2026.
The Roku Channel captured 2.9% of U.S.
TV viewing, placing fifth among streaming services behind YouTube, Netflix, Disney and Amazon Prime Video.
Fox completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, approximately KRW 31.46 trillion, on November 6.
The distinction is how these services reach viewers.
Pluto TV has no television hardware or operating system of its own.
Roku can give The Roku Channel prominent placement across a device and operating-system footprint exceeding 100 million households.
By adding Roku to Tubi, Fox has combined content with access to the TV screen.
Samsung TV Plus and LG Channels, distributed through their manufacturers’ televisions, also rank among the leading U.S.
Skydance is responding by sharing technology with Paramount+ to reduce costs and adding Warner Bros. television hits, including Two and a Half Men, following its Warner Bros. acquisition.
Nearly 35% of streaming users surveyed by Nielsen subsidiary Gracenote said an increasing number of subscription services had led them to spend more time watching FAST.
Platform performance is diverging even as demand for free viewing expands.
Pluto TV’s early appeal was simplicity: open the app and a round-the-clock channel would play without registration or login.
Nielsen first measured its U.S.
TV viewing share at 0.8% in July 2022.
Its share continued rising after reports in July 2024 that Paramount had discussed a sale, reaching a peak of 1% in February 2025.
Nielsen subsequently began reporting Pluto TV together with Paramount+.
Pluto TV’s direction changed after its parent’s merger.
Skydance completed its combination with Paramount in August 2025 and placed former Netflix executive Cindy Holland in charge of both Paramount+ and Pluto TV.
The company set a $2 billion cost-reduction target, approximately KRW 2.86 trillion, and began U.S. layoffs in October.
Vibol Hou, chief product and technology officer for streaming, left at the end of January 2026.
June reports said the two services’ technology integration was progressing toward a launch within the year.
The services would remain separate, with product staff redeployed after completing the integration.
Their quality-assurance teams would also be combined to support AI-based automated testing.
Management was reorganized after the October 6 completion of the Warner Bros.
Announcing a new structure on October 30, Skydance television co-chair JB Perrette said the company was searching internally and externally for a leader for Pluto TV and its AVOD business.
Perrette and DTC chief operating officer Josh Walker oversee the service pending an appointment.
